objective:
Add an `export` command to `stockroom` that turns an orders CSV file into JSON for other tools: `python -m stockroom export --orders FILE [--out PATH] [--status S]... [--customer NAME] [--sort {file,placed,id}] [--limit N]`.

The command reads the orders file exactly as `sales` does. Selection: `--status` may be repeated and each value must be one of `open`, `paid`, `shipped`, `cancelled` (anything else is a usage error); an order is selected when its status is any of the given ones, and without `--status` every status is selected. `--customer NAME` selects the orders whose customer is exactly `NAME` (case-sensitive). When both are given an order must match both. The selected orders are then ordered by `--sort`: `file` (the default) keeps the order in which the orders first appear in the file, `placed` sorts by the date the order was placed, oldest first, and orders placed on the same day by order id, and `id` sorts by order id; order ids compare as plain strings (so `O-10` comes before `O-2`). Finally `--limit N` keeps only the first `N` orders of that sequence; `N` is a whole number of at least 0 (`0` gives no order) and anything else is a usage error.

The output is the JSON text that `stockroom.jsonio.dump_orders` produces for the resulting orders (a JSON list of order objects with sorted keys, indented by 2 spaces, ending with a newline; no orders give `[]` and a newline). Without `--out` it goes to stdout and stderr stays empty.

With `--out PATH` the text is written (UTF-8) to `PATH` instead, stdout stays empty and the exit code is 0. An existing file at `PATH` is replaced, not appended to. The file is replaced atomically: the text is first written to a temporary file in the same directory as `PATH`, which is then renamed over `PATH`, so that at no time a reader sees a partial file and a failure never damages an existing `PATH`. After a run, success or failure, the directory of `PATH` holds no file that was not there before, other than `PATH` itself after a success.

Failures end with exit code 1 and the usual single line `stockroom: error: <reason>` on stderr, with stdout empty: an orders file that is not valid (for example a wrong header), in which case nothing is written and an existing `PATH` keeps its content; a directory of `PATH` that does not exist, and a `PATH` that is an existing directory, in which cases the reason contains `PATH` as given and no file or directory is changed or created.
acceptance: export prints the orders of the file as dump_orders-format JSON (sorted keys, indent 2, trailing newline) in file order by default, with empty stderr and exit code 0; a selection without orders prints '[]'
--status (repeatable, union of the values) and --customer (exact, case-sensitive) select orders, combined with AND; values of --status outside open, paid, shipped, cancelled are usage errors (exit 2)
--sort placed orders by date then order id, --sort id orders by order id as plain strings, --sort file keeps the file order; other values are usage errors
--limit N keeps the first N orders after selection and sorting (0 gives '[]'); a negative or non-integer N is a usage error (exit 2)
--out PATH writes the same text to PATH (replacing existing content, also longer content), prints nothing to stdout and leaves no other file in PATH's directory

An invalid orders file gives exit code 1 and one 'stockroom: error: ' line, writes nothing and leaves an existing --out file unchanged; a missing output directory and an --out that is a directory give exit code 1 with an error line containing the path and leave no stray files
Other commands and their output are unchanged
